title: Nanotopology of Cell Adhesion upon Variable-Angle Total Internal Reflection Fluorescence Microscopy (VA-TIRFM)
protocol: Seed individual cells, e.g., U373-MG or U-251-MG glioblastoma cells at a density of 100 cells/mm² on a glass slide.
Grow cells for 48-72 hours in culture medium (e.g., RPMI 1640 supplemented with 10% fetal calf serum and antibiotics) using an incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO₂.
Incubate cells with a membrane marker, e.g., 6-dodecanoyl-2-dimethylaminonaphthalene (Laurdan), for 60 minutes at a concentration of 8 μM in culture medium.
Wash the cells with culture medium or phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) prior to fluorescence microscopy.
Incubate cells with a cytoplasm marker, e.g., calcein acetoxymethyl ester, for 40 minutes at a concentration of 5 μM in culture medium.
Wash the cells with culture medium or PBS prior to fluorescence microscopy.
Incubate cells with a membrane-associated photosensitizer, e.g., protoporphyrin IX induced by 4 hours incubation with its precursor 5-aminolevulinic acid (ALA; 1 mM).
Wash the cells with culture medium or PBS prior to fluorescence microscopy.
Use an upright microscope, e.g., Zeiss Axioplan.
Replace the condenser with an illumination device as described in a reference.
Optically couple a hemispherical or hemicylindrical glass prism to the object slide.
Use a parallel collimated laser beam which after imaging by the glass prism and further optical components results in a parallel beam on the surface of the sample (telecentric pupil ray).
Ensure that the electrical field vector is polarized perpendicular to the plane of incidence.
Calibrate the angular position of the adjustable mirror using the critical angle Θc=61.3° for a glass-water transition as a fixed value.
Set the parameters of the camera, including temperature, gain, recording time and shift speed.
Localize the object slide in the microscope.
Use immersion oil to assure optical contact of the sample with the glass prism.
Record fluorescence images of identical samples upon variation of the angle of illumination (Θ≥Θc with Θc corresponding to 64.5° for a cell-glass interface).
Use an appropriate long pass or band pass filter for fluorescence detection.
Read images recorded at various angles Θ into the evaluation program.
Input camera settings and excitation wavelength into the evaluation program.
Calculate penetration depth d(Θ) automatically using the provided parameters.
Calculate transmission factor T(Θ) automatically using the provided parameters.
Select images for evaluating cell-substrate distances Δ according to Equation 5 or Equation 4.
Exclude images with inhomogeneous illumination, such as those revealing stripes.
Calculate images of cell-substrate topology and select an appropriate color code for display.
Display profiles of individual pixels during evaluation as indicators of fit quality.
Store the evaluation protocol.
